# Summary of 2005 Political Manifesto

This manifesto presents a comprehensive policy platform centered on environmental sustainability, social equity, and democratic reform.

## Economic Policy

The document proposes restructuring taxation to reduce wealth inequality through progressive tax bands, with higher rates for top earners. It advocates replacing VAT with environmental taxes based on resource usage and pollution. Key economic reforms include introducing Land Value Tax to address land ownership concentration, promoting local economic development through community banks and local currencies, and opposing entry into the single European currency. The manifesto calls for replacing GDP with alternative measures of wellbeing that account for environmental and social factors.

## Energy and Climate

The climate strategy adopts "Contraction and Convergence" principles, targeting 20% carbon dioxide reduction by 2010 and 85% by 2030. Proposals include introducing carbon taxation, increasing renewable energy to 40% by 2020, implementing energy efficiency programmes, and phasing out nuclear power. A cabinet-level position for climate policy is recommended.

## Welfare Reform

Central to welfare policy is a "Citizen's Income" - an unconditional payment to all residents covering basic needs, replacing means-tested benefits. A corresponding "Citizen's Pension" would provide universal retirement income linked to average earnings. The manifesto also addresses housing shortages through local authority investment and self-build cooperatives.

## Public Services

Health policy emphasises prevention and restoring universal NHS principles while opposing privatisation. Proposals include abolishing prescription charges and increasing funding to EU average levels. Education reforms focus on scrapping tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, and abolishing standardised testing for children.

## Transport

Transport policy prioritises sustainable modes over private vehicles, with railways and public transport returned to public ownership. Measures include congestion charging, fuel duty increases, and aviation fuel taxation. A 10% road traffic reduction target is set for 2010.

## Environment and Agriculture

Environmental policy centres on a Zero Waste strategy with 60% recycling targets. The manifesto opposes genetic modification and supports animal welfare legislation. Agricultural reform includes organic production targets of 30% by 2012 and replacing EU agricultural subsidies with support for local food production.

## Crime and Democracy

Crime prevention focuses on community development, increased local policing, and restorative justice approaches. Stricter gun control measures are proposed. Democratic reforms include proportional representation, an elected upper legislative chamber, devolution of power to local government, and opposition to national identity cards.

## International Policy

Foreign policy emphasises diplomacy over military intervention, nuclear disarmament, and increased overseas aid to 1% of national income. The manifesto calls for cancelling debt for the poorest nations, reforming international trade rules to favour local economies, and restructuring EU governance while opposing the proposed EU constitution.
